Models S7 to S10 were next fitted with the observed data. Chain statistics indicated that the HMC algorithm converges with satisfactory results. @fig-chain-stats-s7s10-org shows per-parameter summaries of $\hat{R}$ and effective sample size indicating that parameters have $\hat{R} << 1.01$ and effective sample sizes are generally > 1000 per chain.


```{r}
#| eval: true
#| label: data-prep-obs-fit


d_full <- criteria_dat |> 
  select(participant, time, treat, sex, age, analyte, value) |>
  # Add missing values for all missing obs. 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = value) |> 

  pivot_longer(cols = c(T1, T2, T4), 
               values_to = "value",
               names_to = "time" ) |> 
  
  pivot_wider(names_from = analyte, 
              values_from = value) |> 

    pivot_longer(cols = HDL:Adiponectin, 
               values_to = "value",
               names_to = "analyte" ) |> 
  
  mutate(value_std = if_else(analyte %in% c("TG", "HOMA2IR"), log(value), value)) |> 
  

  
  mutate(.by = analyte, 
         value_std = (value_std - mean(value_std, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(value_std, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 

  mutate(participant = paste0("p", participant)) 



```

# Extract relevant variables for summary statistics
extract_sum <- function(fit) {
  
  all_vars <- fit$metadata()$variables
  keep <- setdiff(
    all_vars,
    grep("^(y|y_rep|y_expect|y_impute|pre|pre_impute|pre_wide|
                 y_wide_1|y_wide_2|mu_wide_1|mu_wide_2|mu|sig|
                 log_lik_part|diagnosed|n_criteria)\\[",
         all_vars, value = TRUE)
  )
  sum <- fit$summary(variables = keep, .cores = 12)
  return(sum)
  
}

fits <- list(fit.s7.post, 
             fit.s8.post, 
             fit.s9.post, 
             fit.s10.post)

# Extracting chain diagnostics takes some time - Only this if refit.models == TRUE
# and/or chain diagnostics isn't available. 
if(!(file.exists("./data-derived/chain-diagnostics-s7-s10.RDS") & refit.models)) {
  sums <- lapply(fits, extract_sum)
  models <- paste0("s", 7:10)
  
  for(i in 1:4) {
    sums[[i]] <- sums[[i]] |> 
    mutate(model = models[i])
  }
  
  saveRDS(sums, "./data-derived/chain-diagnostics-s7-s10.RDS")
  
} else {
  sums <- readRDS("./data-derived/chain-diagnostics-s7-s10.RDS")
}

  labs(x = "Effective sample size (ESS Bulk)", 
       y = "Rhat", 
       size = "ESS tail")

Using the observed data set we are next assessing the models tendencies to produce replicated data similar to the observed data. All models (s7-s10) are still considered in these posterior predictive checks. The overall distributions of replicated data (y^rep^) tend to look very similar to the observed data for each measurement type, treatment, and time-point combinations, both for all models model S7 (@fig-ppcheck-dist).

# Distribution of observed values vs. distribution of y rep
ppcheck_dist <- function(yreps, obsdata, label = FALSE) {
  
  # For the caption 
  caption <- str_wrap(paste("Type labels: ", 
                   paste0(labels$type, ",", labels$label, collapse = "; ")))
  
  
  
  # Set number of draws for posterior predictive checks
  # and sample from random draw
  ndraws <- 40
  randraw <- sample(1:(max(yreps$.draw)), ndraws)
  
  p <- yreps |> 
  filter(.draw %in% randraw) |> 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("y_rep")) |> 
  mutate(
    miss_pre = rep(d$pre_miss, ndraws),
    miss = rep(d$y_miss, ndraws),
    type = rep(d$type, ndraws), 
    sex = rep(ifelse(d$sex == -0.5, "m", "f"), ndraws),
    treat = rep(d$treat, ndraws), 
    time = rep(d$time, ndraws),
  ) |> 
    # Filter simulations not corresponding to observed data
    # Filter away missing data obs
    filter(miss == 1, 
           miss_pre == 1) |> 
    
  ggplot(aes(value)) + 
  geom_line(stat = "density", 
            aes(color = sex, group = paste(.draw, sex)),
            alpha = 0.2) + 
  facet_grid(time + treat ~ type, 
             labeller = label_both) +
  
  geom_line(data = obsdata, 
            aes(y, group = NULL, color = sex), 
            stat = "density", 
     
            alpha = 0.8,
            linewidth = 1.2) +
  alpha_theme(yaxis = FALSE) + 
    scale_color_manual(values = colscale[c(1, 3)]) +
  theme(axis.title.y =  element_blank()) + 
    labs(x = "y^rep^ and observed values", 
         color = "Sex")  +
    theme(axis.title.x = element_markdown(), 
          axis.title.y = element_blank()) 
  
  if(label) {
    p <- p + labs(caption = caption)
            }
  
  return(p)
  
}

p1 <- ppcheck_dist(yrep.s7, dobs) + labs(subtitle = "Model s7")

p2 <- ppcheck_dist(yrep.s8, dobs)+ labs(subtitle = "Model s8")

p3 <- ppcheck_dist(yrep.s9, dobs)+ labs(subtitle = "Model s9")

To further explore model implications we calculate the observed standard deviations per measurement type and sex and extract distributions implied by the model through y^rep^. In @fig-ppcheck-s7-sd and @fig-ppcheck-s8-sd most distributions of y^rep^ standard deviations contain the empirical standard deviation, however, for both model S7 and S8 the standard deviations observed in the data do not correspond to those implied by the model. 

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppcheck-s7-sd
#| fig-cap: "Posterior predictive check of model s7. The distributions of standard deviations calculated from y^rep^"
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 8
#| eval: false



# Obs data (make sure sex is sorted cerrectly)
dobs <- data.frame(
  
  miss = d$y_miss,
  miss_pre = d$pre_miss,
  pre = d$pre_obs,
  y = d$y_obs, 
  type = d$type, 
    sex = factor(ifelse(d$sex == -0.5, "m", "f"), levels = c("m", "f")),
    treat = d$treat, 
  time = d$time
  ) |> 
    # Filter away missing data obs
    filter(miss == 1, 
           miss_pre == 1) 


# Posterior predictive check. the function can be used for a summary statistics
# function (sd, mean, max, min, quantile).
# use stat_arg for supplying extra functions to the summary function.
ppcheck_stat <- function(yreps, obsdata, stat = sd, stat_arg = list(),
                         group = c("type", "time", "treat", "sex"),
                         fill_color = "sex", 
                         plot = TRUE) {

  if (obsdata$sex[1] %in% c(-0.5, 0.5)) stop("Convert sex to a factor with 'm' and 'f'")
  if (!fill_color %in% group) stop("`fill_color` must be one of `group`")

  sumstat <- obsdata |>
    summarise(.by = all_of(group),
              s = do.call(stat, c(list(y), stat_arg)))

  ndraws <- nrow(yreps)
  caption <- paste("Type labels: ",
                   paste0(labels$type, ", ", labels$label, collapse = ";\n"))

  y_rep_data <- yreps |>
    filter(.draw %in% 1:ndraws) |>
    pivot_longer(starts_with("y_rep")) |>
    mutate(
      miss     = rep(d$y_miss,   ndraws),
      miss_pre = rep(d$pre_miss, ndraws),
      type     = rep(d$type,     ndraws),
      sex      = rep(ifelse(d$sex == -0.5, "m", "f"), ndraws),
      treat    = rep(d$treat,    ndraws),
      time     = rep(d$time,     ndraws),
      sex      = factor(sex, levels = c("m", "f"))
    ) |>
    filter(miss == 1, miss_pre == 1) |>
    summarise(.by = all_of(c(".draw", group)),
              s = do.call(stat, c(list(value), stat_arg)))

  pvals <- y_rep_data |>
    rename(srep = s) |>
    inner_join(sumstat) |>
    summarise(.by = all_of(group), pval = mean(srep >= s)) |>
    mutate(direction = if_else(pval > 0.5, "over", "under"),
           pval = pmin(pval, 1 - pval)) |>
    arrange(pval)

  if(plot) {
     plot1 <- y_rep_data |>
    ggplot(aes(s, fill = .data[[fill_color]])) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25) +
    facet_grid(type ~ time + treat, labeller = label_both, scales = "free") +
    alpha_theme(yaxis = FALSE) +
    geom_vline(data = sumstat,
               aes(xintercept = s, color = .data[[fill_color]])) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colscale) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colscale) +
    labs(x = "Test statistic",
         color = fill_color, fill = fill_color,
         subtitle = "Estimates (T(y^rep^) and T(y^obs^))",
         caption = caption) +
    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(),
          plot.subtitle = element_markdown())

  plot2 <- y_rep_data |>
    rename(srep = s) |>
    inner_join(sumstat) |>
    mutate(t_diff = srep - s) |>
    ggplot(aes(t_diff, fill = .data[[fill_color]])) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25) +
    facet_grid(type ~ time + treat, labeller = label_both, scales = "free") +
    alpha_theme(yaxis = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colscale) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colscale) +
    labs(x = "Contrast", fill = fill_color,
         subtitle = "Contrast (T(y^rep^) - T(y^obs^))",
         caption = caption) +
    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(),
          plot.subtitle = element_markdown())
  
  return(list(plot_estimate = plot1, plot_contrast = plot2, pvals = pvals))
  
  } else {
    return(pvals)
  }
 

  
}

# Extract participants with no missing values

  part = d$P,

no_miss_part <- paste0("log_lik_part[", no_miss_part, "]")


library(loo)

loo_routine <- function(fit, vars) {
  
  log_lik_mat <- fit$draws(variables = vars, format = "matrix")  # iters x N_P
  
  r_eff <- relative_eff(exp(log_lik_mat),
                        chain_id = rep(1:fit$num_chains(),
                                       each = fit$metadata()$iter_sampling))
  
  loo1 <- loo(log_lik_mat, r_eff = r_eff, save_psis = TRUE)
  return(loo1)
  
}

  s11 = loo.s11,

  s13 = loo.s13 )), simplify = FALSE)
  

print(loo_compare(list(
  s8 = loo.s8,

  s10 = loo.s10,
  s11 = loo.s11,
  s12 = loo.s12)), simplify = FALSE)

plot(loo.s12)



## Plotting observed data and 
# Obs data (make sure sex is sorted cerrectly)
dobs <- data.frame(
  P = d$P,
  miss = d$y_miss,
  miss_pre = d$pre_miss,
  pre = d$pre_obs,
  y = d$y_obs, 
  type = d$type, 
    sex = factor(ifelse(d$sex == -0.5, "m", "f"), levels = c("m", "f")),
    treat = d$treat, 
  time = d$time
  ) |> 
    # Filter away missing data obs
    filter(miss == 1, 
           miss_pre == 1) 

# Extract participants with no missing values
no_miss_part <- data.frame(
  part = d$P,
  y_miss = d$y_miss,
  pre_miss = d$pre_miss
) |> 
  summarise(.by = part, 
            y = sum(y_miss), 
            pre = sum(pre_miss)) |> 
  filter(y == 20,
         pre == 20) |> 
  pull(part) 

pointwise <- loo.s12$pointwise |> 
  data.frame() |> 
  rownames_to_column(var = "P") |> 
  mutate(P = gsub("log_lik_part\\[|\\]","", P), 
         P = as.integer(P)) |> 
  print()


dobs |> 
  filter(P %in% no_miss_part) |> 
  # add pareto K estimates
  inner_join(pointwise) |> 
  mutate(flag = if_else(influence_pareto_k > 0.7, "high", "low")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(pre, y, color = flag)) + geom_point(aes(alpha = flag)) + 
  facet_wrap(type ~ time, labeller = label_both) + 
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(0.9, 0.3))









```

























### Archive



```{r}
#| eval: false
#| label: fig-ppcheck-s8-sd
#| fig-cap: "Posterior predictive check of model s8. The distributions of standard deviations calculated from y^rep^"
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 8

# New number of draws
ndraws <- 1000

sumstat <- dobs |> 
    summarise(.by = c(type, time, treat),
            s = sd(y)) 

# Statistics vs observed

yrep.s8 |> 
  filter(.iteration %in% 1:ndraws) |> 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("y_rep")) |> 
  mutate(
    type = rep(d$type, ndraws * 4), 
    sex = rep(d$sex, ndraws * 4),
    treat = rep(d$treat, ndraws * 4),
    time = rep(d$time, ndraws * 4)
  ) |> 
  summarise(.by = c(.iteration, type, time, treat),
            s = sd(value)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(s)) + geom_histogram() + 
  facet_grid(type ~ time + treat, 
             labeller = label_both) + 
  alpha_theme(yaxis = FALSE) + 
  
  geom_vline(data = sumstat, 
             aes(xintercept = s, color = as.factor(treat))) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale) + 
  labs(x = "Standard deviation", 
       color = "Treatment") + 
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())


```

Similarly to posterior predictive checks of the standard deviations, comparing percentiles (5% and 95%) between y^rep^ and observed data indicate that the observed data overlap with posterior distributions in most cases. Again, however, some measurements types (e.g., type 7) indicate imabalønce between treatments.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| label: fig-ppcheck-s8-quantiles
#| fig-cap: "Posterior predictive check of model s8. The distributions of percentiles (5 and 95%) calculated from y^rep^"
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 8

# New number of draws
ndraws <- 1000

sumstat <- dobs |> 
    summarise(.by = c(type, time, treat),
            q5 = quantile(y, 0.05), 
            q95 = quantile(y, 0.95))  |> 
  pivot_longer(names_to = "stat", 
               values_to = "value", 
               cols = q5:q95) 

# Statistics vs observed

yrep.s8 |> 
  filter(.iteration %in% 1:ndraws) |> 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("y_rep")) |> 
  mutate(
    type = rep(d$type, ndraws * 4), 
    sex = rep(d$sex, ndraws * 4),
    treat = rep(d$treat, ndraws * 4),
    time = rep(d$time, ndraws * 4)
  ) |> 
  summarise(.by = c(.iteration, type, time, treat),
            q5 = quantile(value, 0.05), 
            q95 = quantile(value, 0.95)) |> 
    pivot_longer(names_to = "stat", 
               values_to = "value", 
               cols = q5:q95) |> 
  
  ggplot(aes(value, fill = stat)) + geom_histogram() + 
  facet_grid(type ~ time + treat, 
             labeller = label_both) + 
  alpha_theme(yaxis = FALSE) + 
  
  geom_vline(data = sumstat, 
             aes(xintercept = value, color = stat)) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = colscale) + 
  labs(x = "Quantiles (5% and 95%)", 
       color = "", 
       fill = "") + 
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())


```



Together, the posterior predictive check indicate that, for some cases of measurement types, the model implied variation among replicated data do not overlap with the observed data. As both models S7 and S8 assumes equal variation between treatments a natural extension of both models is to add treatment-specific variation. Models S9 and S10 incorporates this addition.
